record.paper_title: Mapping Class Group Factorizations and Symplectic 4-Manifolds: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Map_{g,n} be the mapping class group of a genus-g surface with n greater than 0 boundary components, and let delta be the boundary twist, the product of positive Dehn twists parallel to the boundary components. Under the relative-minimality assumption that every component of every reducible singular fiber intersects at least one distinguished section, is there an a priori upper bound on the length of any factorization of delta as a product of positive Dehn twists in Map_{g,n}? Equivalently, is there a genus-only upper bound on the number of singular fibers of a Lefschetz fibration admitting a section of square -1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_{g,n}$ denote a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n\ge 1$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ be its mapping class group (isotopy classes of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms fixing the boundary pointwise). Let $\delta\in\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ be the boundary multitwist, i.e. the product of the right-handed Dehn twists along $n$ disjoint simple closed curves each parallel to one of the boundary components.

A positive factorization of $\delta$ is an expression $\delta = \tau_{c_1}\tau_{c_2}\cdots\tau_{c_k}$, where each $\tau_{c_i}$ is a right-handed Dehn twist along a simple closed curve $c_i\subset\Sigma_{g,n}$. Each such factorization gives rise to a genus-$g$ Lefschetz fibration $f: X \to D^2$ over the disk with $n$ distinguished sections, where the number $k$ of factors equals the number of singular fibers, and each distinguished section has self-intersection $-1$ exactly when $n=1$ and the boundary twist factor structure is interpreted accordingly. Call the factorization relatively minimal if every irreducible component of every reducible singular fiber of the associated Lefschetz fibration intersects at least one of the distinguished sections (equivalently, no vanishing cycle bounds a disk disjoint from the sections).

Question. Fix $g\ge 1$ and $n\ge 1$. Does there exist a constant $C(g,n)$ depending only on $g$ and $n$ such that every relatively minimal positive factorization of $\delta$ in $\mathrm{Map}_{g,n}$ has length at most $C(g,n)$?

Equivalently: is the number of singular fibers of a relatively minimal genus-$g$ Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admitting a section of self-intersection $-1$ bounded above by a function depending only on the genus $g$?
artifact.category_tag: Lefschetz fibrations and mapping class group factorizations
artifact.status_search_result: The question (attributed to Ivan Smith) asks for a genus-only upper bound on the length of positive factorizations of the boundary twist under a relative minimality hypothesis involving a section of square -1. Without the relative-minimality/section-square-(-1) hypothesis, Baykur–Korkmaz and others have shown that for $g\ge 3$ arbitrarily long positive factorizations of boundary multitwists exist, but these constructions do not satisfy the relative-minimality condition. No source found establishes or refutes a genus-only bound in the relatively minimal setting with a $-1$ section; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Mapping class group factorizations and symplectic 4-manifolds: some open problems (Auroux)
status_evidence.snippet: Question (Smith): Is there an a priori upper bound on the length of any factorization of the boundary twist as a product of positive Dehn twists?
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Arbitrarily Long Factorizations in Mapping Class Groups (Baykur–Korkmaz et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: For g >= 3, the boundary multitwist admits positive factorizations of arbitrarily large length.
status_evidence.claim: Without the relative-minimality hypothesis, no such bound exists for g >= 3, but these factorizations are not relatively minimal.

status_evidence.title: A note on the topology of Lefschetz fibrations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses relatively minimal Lefschetz fibrations and sections of square -1; no genus-only upper bound on the number of singular fibers is asserted in the relatively minimal case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature still treats the bound as not established.
